Rishi / Monica —

QuantifyAI (deal QNTFY-2026-114) moved to commercial review last night. Sales asked for a firm sizing + any provisional node hold we can offer for the first 90 days of onboarding. Key ask from account team: predictable tail-latency under a 99th percentile SLA and a short runway to scale from POC -> 10k gen/min within 60 days.

Can Ops do a quick inventory/fit assessment and highlight any thermal-affinity or SKU limitations that would impact a soft-hold? I attached a snapshot export (node_inventory_snapshot_20260503.csv) and a recent thermal bin report. Please call out:
- Minimum node count to hit target throughput with 95ms avg gen latency (approx 4096 token average)
- Thermal bin mapping (which racks/regions we should avoid or mark lower-priority)
- Anything that would prevent a 14-day soft-reserve (hot standby) starting 2026-06-01

If we can, propose a conservative provisional hold (not contractually binding) that sales can present to Quantify.

Thanks —
Markus
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: QuantifyAI late-stage node-fit & thermal mapping

Markus —

Thanks for the heads up. I pulled the attached CSV and did a quick pass. Short summary up front: we have N+ spare in the us-west pool but about 18% of capacity is on high-thermal racks (bin C) which will degrade sustained throughput if we rely on long Llama-style sequences. Preliminary numbers (ballpark):

- For 10k gen/min with 4k avg tokens and 95ms p50 target, we need ~28 A100s at baseline using our current kernel set. With quantization and batching optimizations we can push that down to ~22 GPUs.
- Given thermal bins, to guarantee the 99p latency SLO I'd recommend reserving 32 GPUs on mixed racks with at least 24 in bin A/B.
- 14-day soft-reserve starting 2026-06-01: operationally feasible if sales accepts a ‘best-effort’ hold that we convert to a dedicated pool once the contract and commit are signed. I can hold a tag on the node pool in the scheduler (non-blocking) and then escalate to a binding allocation with SRE if we get a PO.

Risks / caveats:
- If Quantify pushes longer context runs or sampling-heavy load during onboarding, we may need to swap to higher-memory GPUs (e.g., 80GB) which are scarcer.
- Network egress patterns: they plan large batched embeddings in week 2 of onboarding — need to confirm whether those run on the same fleet (could create transient saturation).

I'll attach a short thermal mapping export and a suggested provisional hold message for Sales. If you want, I can also run a trace simulation against their expected QPS (send me the exact prompt mix) and turn this into a short MAP entry.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

- VPC peering & egress: if they want embeddings batched outbound we'll carve a separate egress lane and quota; that needs a network ticket but it’s low friction.
- Attach MAP_QuantifyAI_v2.docx — I updated the onboarding checklist with steps that touch infra (KMS, peering, firewall rules).

Operational suggestion: mark the provisional nodes as "standby:quantifyai" in the scheduler and set an expiration of 14 days by default. If Sales wants an extension, we'll treat it as a contract trigger.

—Monica

1) Context lengths: our POC uses ~1k tokens, but the production plan includes recurring batches up to 6k tokens for summarization workloads. We expect ~70% of requests to be short (<=1k) and 30% long (4k-6k).

3) Timeline: we are targeting production traffic ramp beginning 2026-06-20. Can you confirm a conservative provisional reserve that supports the mixed context profile?

Also, procurement sent a short checklist (attached in their next email). If you can return a one-page provisioning commitment (non-binding) we can attach it to our internal procurement memo.
